title: A story whose goal names answer quality gets a held-out quality probe as its premise before the sprint starts
goal: At /kb-sprint plan, a committed story whose goal names a quality of answers (an answer rate, a verdict's accuracy, a ranking) records as its Premise a probe of that quality on held-out inputs (such as rag.py eval --file on questions the work will not tune on), run before the start gate is asked, so a gate the probe raises is asked before start, not mid-work. Answers the SP-njilrify retrospective: the accuracy gate of ST-dvf3xf52 came mid-work when a held-out run answered 14 of 20 with verdict good on all 20, and research story ST-ulhmplqh had to be filed in the sprint; the plan premise had only shown coverage none.

gates.question: How is the held-out quality premise enforced at sprint plan?
options: rule text: kb-sprint plan step 6, kb-backlog Plan and kb/_self/backlog.md Sprints ask for the probe; no tool change

tool warning: backlog.py check warns of a committed story whose goal names a quality figure and whose notes hold no Premise line running a probe (adds _tools/bl_*.py check code and its docs to the touches)
gates.recommendation: rule text: kb-sprint plan step 6, kb-backlog Plan and kb/_self/backlog.md Sprints ask for the probe; no tool change

notes: Premise: the SP-njilrify history; ST-ulhmplqh's notes (git history) record the held-out run (rag.py eval --file of 20 held-out rule questions --root _self: 14 passed, verdict good on all 20) that raised the accuracy gate of ST-dvf3xf52 after work began. selfdoc.py check passes before the work: it pins that no heading reference goes dead when the skills change. Touches agents-rule paths (.claude/skills/): how the rule is enforced is an operator gate.
